title: Small-quench Loschmidt dynamics near quantum critical points
abstract: We study the short-time Loschmidt dynamics after a small sudden quench near a quantum critical point. We show that the initial quadratic growth of the Loschmidt rate function is governed by the variance of the quench operator per system size. For a local quench operator, this variance density is exactly equal to the spatial sum of the equal-time connected two-point correlation function in the initial ground state. This relation connects the early-time Loschmidt response to static critical correlations. Assuming power-law correlations at criticality, we classify the finite-size scaling of the short-time coefficient by the scaling dimension of the quench operator. In one dimension, the coefficient is finite, logarithmically enhanced, or algebraically enhanced with system size. We illustrate this operator dependence in the transverse-field Ising chain, where transverse-field and longitudinal-field quenches couple to different critical operators. We also discuss the first correction beyond the quadratic regime using the fourth cumulant of the post-quench Hamiltonian.
summary: This paper analyzes the initial decay of the Loschmidt echo after a small quench near a quantum critical point. It establishes that the initial decay rate is governed by the variance of the quench operator, which is directly related to static critical correlations. The work provides detailed scaling laws showing how this early-time response depends on the dimensionality and the scaling dimension of the quench operator.
main_problem: The paper investigates the initial growth rate of the Loschmidt rate function following a small sudden quench near a quantum critical point (QCP). It aims to connect this early-time dynamic response to static critical correlations.
main_result: The initial quadratic coefficient of the Loschmidt decay is exactly determined by the spatial sum of the equal-time connected two-point correlation function of the quench operator. The finite-size scaling of this coefficient depends critically on the scaling dimension of the quench operator relative to the system dimension.
method: The analysis uses the short-time cumulant expansion of the Loschmidt amplitude, relating the quadratic coefficient to the variance of the quench operator and analyzing the scaling of this variance using critical correlation functions.
model_or_system: The study applies to quantum many-body systems, specifically illustrating results using the transverse-field Ising chain model subjected to small quenches (e.g., changing the transverse or longitudinal field).
key_observables: Loschmidt rate function $f(t)$, initial quadratic coefficient $\chi_V$, and higher-order cumulants ($\kappa_4$).
important_parameters: System size ($L$), quench operator scaling dimension ($\Delta$), and the small quench parameter ($\delta\lambda$ or $\delta h$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the small-quench approximation and assumes power-law decay for critical correlations, $C(r) \sim |r|^{-2\Delta}$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the connection between the short-time Loschmidt dynamics and the variance of the quench operator. It then derives the scaling laws for this variance based on critical exponents and analyzes the crossover behavior by including the fourth cumulant correction.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework linking the non-equilibrium dynamics (Loschmidt echo) directly to the static properties (critical correlations) of the ground state, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum criticality in many-body systems.
